key_insight: Advanced energy management delivers modest savings in electrified Belgian homes: €82.5/year for TreeC and €116.6/year for MPC versus default-like control.
engineering_relevance: MPC maximizes practical savings, while TreeC offers higher EV charge completion and smoother aggregate demand, creating a cost–performance trade-off for home energy control.
method: Simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings with heat pumps, electric boilers, EV chargers, and photovoltaics assigned at current adoption rates.
Compare decision-tree control (TreeC) and model predictive control (MPC) against rule-based control and perfect-forecast MPC.
Evaluate 2023 operation under hourly electricity prices and a monthly peak tariff.
evidence_signal: Simulations show similar thermal comfort across controllers; TreeC achieves 93.3% EV charge completion versus 88.8% for MPC, while perfect-forecast MPC saves €177.4/year.
watch_item: Savings may not justify €280–680 purchase costs plus €0–360/year subscriptions; results reflect simulated homes and one year of Belgian tariff conditions.
paper_title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?
